Story file: - docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md exists with requirements and acceptance criteria for ESLint configuration presets, flat config, customizable paths, rule options, integration, and config validation.
Core functionality – recommended & strict presets (REQ-CONFIG-PRESETS, Core Functionality): - src/index.ts: - Defines TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES mapping traceability/* rules to severities. - createTraceabilityFlatConfig() returns a flat-config fragment: - `{ plugins: { traceability: {} }, rules: { ...TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES } }`. - Exposes presets: `const configs = { recommended: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()], strict: [createTraceabilityFlatConfig()] };`. - tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts: - Verifies plugin default export includes rules and configs. - Verifies rules object has all expected rule names. - Test "[REQ-RULE-REGISTRY] configs.recommended contains correct rule configuration" checks the recommended preset rules and severities. - Test "[REQ-CONFIG-SYSTEM] configs.strict contains same rules as recommended" asserts strict and recommended presets match. - docs/config-presets.md: - Documents `traceability.configs.recommended` and `traceability.configs.strict`. - Provides example eslint.config.js usage for each preset.
ESLint v9 flat config support & best practices (REQ-FLAT-CONFIG, Quality Standards): - eslint.config.js: - CommonJS flat config exporting an array of config objects via `module.exports = [ ... ]`. - Uses `@eslint/js` flat configs via `const js = require("@eslint/js");` and `js.configs.recommended` at the top of the array. - Provides dedicated blocks for: - Node.js config files (CommonJS, with appropriate globals). - TypeScript files using @typescript-eslint/parser with `project` and `tsconfigRootDir`. - JavaScript files. - Test files with Jest globals. - Ignores block for lib, node_modules, coverage, docs, markdown, etc. - Header comment explicitly ties this file to the story: - `@story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md` - `@req REQ-FLAT-CONFIG - Setup ESLint v9 flat config for plugin usage`. - README.md: - States ESLint v9+ as prerequisite. - Quick Start shows flat-config usage: `export default [traceability.configs.recommended];`. - References user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md for detailed ESLint 9 setup. - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md: - Extensive documentation on ESLint 9 flat config: array-of-objects structure, using js.configs.recommended, ignores, no extends. - Provides working examples (JS-only, TS, mixed JS/TS, Node configs, tests, monorepos) aligned with ESLint v9 best practices.
Customizable story paths & rule options (REQ-CUSTOMIZABLE-PATHS, REQ-RULE-OPTIONS): - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts: - Supports configurable options via meta.schema: - `storyDirectories: { type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }`. - `allowAbsolutePaths: { type: "boolean" }`. - `requireStoryExtension: { type: "boolean" }`. - `additionalProperties: false`. - Default behavior and option handling: - `const defaultStoryDirs = ["docs/stories", "stories"];`. - Reads options from `context.options[0]` and computes: - `const storyDirs = opts?.storyDirectories || defaultStoryDirs;` - `const allowAbsolute = opts?.allowAbsolutePaths || false;` - `const requireExt = opts?.requireStoryExtension !== false;`. - These values drive validateStoryPath/processStoryPath and downstream filesystem checks, enabling customization of story paths while enforcing constraints. - src/utils/storyReferenceUtils.ts: - `buildStoryCandidates(storyPath, cwd, storyDirs)` uses the provided storyDirs array to construct candidate file paths, implementing customizable story directories. - Boundary checks and existence checks respect these directories while ensuring security and project-boundary constraints. - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts: - meta.schema for rule options: - `scope: { type: "array", items: { type: "string", enum: DEFAULT_SCOPE }, uniqueItems: true }`. - `exportPriority: { type: "string", enum: EXPORT_PRIORITY_VALUES }`. - `additionalProperties: false`. - create() reads options via `const opts = (context.options && context.options[0]) || {};`, defaulting scope and exportPriority when not provided, implementing configurable rule options.
Configuration validation & error handling of invalid options (REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION, Error Handling): - Rule-level JSON Schema validation: - src/rules/valid-story-reference.ts meta.schema: - Defines types for storyDirectories, allowAbsolutePaths, requireStoryExtension. - `additionalProperties: false` ensures unknown configuration keys result in ESLint schema validation errors instead of being silently ignored. - src/rules/require-story-annotation.ts meta.schema: - Defines `scope` and `exportPriority` with enum values. - `additionalProperties: false` disallows unknown options. - Tests tied to this story validate configuration schemas and validation behavior: - tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts: - Header: `/** @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md */`. - `it("[REQ-RULE-OPTIONS] rule meta.schema defines expected properties", ...)` asserts valid-story-reference.meta.schema[0].properties includes `storyDirectories`, `allowAbsolutePaths`, and `requireStoryExtension`. - `it("[REQ-CONFIG-VALIDATION] schema disallows unknown options", ...)` asserts `schema.additionalProperties` is `false`. - tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts: - Header: `/** @story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md */`. - `it("[REQ-RULE-OPTIONS] require-story-annotation schema defines expected properties", ...)` asserts meta.schema[0].properties includes `scope` and `exportPriority`, and `additionalProperties` is `false`. - Together these schemas and tests ensure invalid configuration options are rejected with clear, ESLint-native schema error messages instead of failing mysteriously or being ignored.
Project integration for JS/TS/mixed projects (REQ-PROJECT-INTEGRATION, Integration): - eslint.config.js demonstrates real-world integration of the plugin into a TypeScript-heavy plugin project: - Base: `js.configs.recommended`. - Node.js config files block for *.config.js, *.config.mjs, jest.config.js with CommonJS sourceType and necessary globals. - TypeScript block for "**/*.ts", "**/*.tsx": - Uses @typescript-eslint/parser with project/tsconfigRootDir. - Attaches plugin via `plugins: { ...(plugin.rules ? { traceability: plugin } : {}) }`. - JavaScript block for "**/*.js", "**/*.jsx" with plugin and maintainability rules. - Test files block specifying Jest globals, turning off complexity/max-lines rules to keep tests flexible. - Ignores for lib, node_modules, coverage, docs, markdown, and tooling directories. - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md: - Provides configuration patterns for JS-only, TS-only, mixed JS/TS, Node config files, tests, and monorepos. - Shows how to integrate the plugin’s configs with @eslint/js in consumer projects. - tests/integration/cli-integration.test.ts: - Uses ESLint CLI with `--no-config-lookup --config eslint.config.js` and dynamically resolves the ESLint CLI binary. - Runs ESLint against inline code via stdin with plugin rules like traceability/require-story-annotation and traceability/valid-req-reference. - Verifies expected process exit statuses, demonstrating that ESLint, the flat config, and this plugin interact correctly in a CLI scenario.
User experience & documentation (User Experience, Documentation acceptance criteria): - README.md: - Installation instructions and prerequisites (Node.js >=14, ESLint v9+). - Quick Start example showing how to include `traceability.configs.recommended` in eslint.config.js. - Lists available rules and links to detailed rule docs in docs/rules/. - Links to user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md, user-docs/api-reference.md, user-docs/examples.md, and user-docs/migration-guide.md. - user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md: - Detailed configuration examples for different project types (JavaScript, TypeScript, mixed, monorepos). - Troubleshooting section for flat config issues and common ESLint 9 problems. - Working example for a TypeScript ESLint plugin project that closely mirrors this repository’s structure. - docs/config-presets.md: - Explains recommended vs strict presets, their rule severities, and how to include them in flat config. - These documents provide clear setup guidance, configuration examples, and troubleshooting information for common project types, satisfying the user experience and documentation acceptance criteria.
Traceability to this story: - Tests explicitly reference this story: - tests/config/eslint-config-validation.test.ts and tests/config/require-story-annotation-config.test.ts both include `@story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md` and describe blocks clearly labeled for Story 002.0. - eslint.config.js is annotated with `@story docs/stories/002.0-DEV-ESLINT-CONFIG.story.md`. - Rule schemas for configuration options are tested in Story 002.0-specific test files.
